b1-unit-14.14.1 Dinner is on me:
Danny: So, this is the place. Bruno says it's the best bistro in town.
Ana: It looks lovely. And you look much better than last week!
Danny: I feel great. That's why we're here. You were my doctor, so tonight dinner is on me.
Waiter: Good evening. Are you ready to order, or do you need a few more minutes?
Danny: I think we're ready. Could you tell me what today's special is?
Waiter: Of course. It's grilled salmon with an almond butter sauce.
Danny: Oh, I'm allergic to nuts. And do you know if the risotto has any nuts in it?
Waiter: No, the mushroom risotto is nut-free. But I don't recommend the salmon for you.
Danny: Thanks. Then I'll have the steak. What does it come with?
Waiter: It comes with fries or mashed potatoes, and a side salad.
Danny: Mashed potatoes, please.
Waiter: How would you like your steak?
Danny: Medium, please.
Waiter: And which dressing would you like on your salad? We have Caesar or oil and vinegar.
Danny: Oil and vinegar, please.
Waiter: Very good. And for you, ma'am?
Ana: I'd like to start with the tomato soup. And for my main course, I'll have the mushroom risotto.
Waiter: Excellent choice. Anything to drink?
Danny: I'll have a lemonade. No, wait... make that an iced tea.
Ana: Just water for me, please. Sparkling, if you have it.
Waiter: Certainly.
Ana: Danny, do you know what medium means exactly? I never know what to say, and I didn't want to ask.
Danny: Medium is pink in the middle. Rare is red inside, and well-done is cooked all the way through.
Waiter: Did you enjoy your meal? Can I get you some dessert? I can recommend the chocolate cake. It's homemade.
Ana: No, thanks. I'm completely full. I don't think I have room for anything else.
Danny: Me too. Could we have the check, please?
Waiter: Of course. Just a moment.
Ana: Let me get this, Danny. You're on a gap year!
Danny: No, no. It's on me. You saved my life last week.
Ana: You had the flu, Danny. You didn't need saving! But OK, if you insist. Next time is on me.
Danny: Deal. Hey, the check says ten percent service. Do you know if I should leave a tip too?
Ana: In Brazil, that ten percent is the tip. It's optional, but people usually pay it when the service is good.
Danny: The service was great. I'll pay it. Back home, my mom always leaves twenty percent!

Narrator: Do you know if it's spicy?
